author: historian-agent:gemini-flash-outline
title: Origin of human language
summary: When human language began is not settled. Bolhuis and colleagues argue that evidence from human prehistory suggests the faculty of language emerged some 70,000 to 100,000 years ago, which they say fits a simple definition of syntax. The Smithsonian notes that many advanced traits, including complex symbolic expression, art and elaborate cultural diversity, emerged mainly during the past 100,000 years.

uncertainty.note: Chronology spans the proposed emergence window of modern syntactic language in Africa (c. 100,000–70,000 years ago) correlated with the earliest indisputable symbolic artifact assemblages.

as_recorded.value: the faculty of language emerged some 70,000–100,000 years ago
Many advanced traits -- including complex symbolic expression, art, and elaborate cultural diversity -- emerged mainly during the past 100,000 years

where.modern_name: No single place; stand-in pin at Blombos Cave, South Africa
where.historical_name: Southern African coastal savanna, Middle Stone Age; no human polities existed

importance.justification: The emergence of recursive syntactic communication fundamentally restructured human sociality, thought, and information sharing, making cumulative human culture possible.

related.because: Complex linguistic communication and symbolic coordination enabled modern human bands to organize long-range migrations across new continents.

sources.title: Language: UG or Not to Be, That Is the Question (PLOS Biology 13:e1002063)
sources.author: Johan J. Bolhuis, Ian Tattersall, Noam Chomsky, Robert C. Berwick

sources.title: Introduction to Human Evolution
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, Human Origins Program
sources.author: Smithsonian Human Origins Program

reviewer_note: The date comes from one research team, and speech leaves no direct fossils. The pin is a stand-in at Blombos Cave, which has its own record for engraved ochre.
